description: A snare drum: a tuned body with a short pitch drop, and a band of noise for the wires

params.text: Sets the frequency the body settles to, from 100Hz to 400Hz
Sets how long the drum takes to fade, from 0.05 to 0.8 seconds
Sets how far above the settled frequency the body starts, reaching 200Hz at its maximum
Sets the level of the noise layer that makes the wire rattle
Multiplies the whole drum before a soft clipper, from unity at its minimum to six times at its maximum
Sets how long the pitch drop takes, from 5ms to 100ms

inputs.text: A rising edge fires the drum, restarting the envelopes, the phase of the body and the noise filter
Raises the body an octave per volt, on top of the frequency knob

outputs.text: The drum, soft-clipped and peaking at ±5V

notes: nothing comes out until a trigger arrives; between hits the module puts each channel to sleep and holds it at 0V.
the noise fades at half the rate of the body, so the wires ring on after the drum has gone.
the lamp lights for about a tenth of a second on each trigger and switches off cleanly rather than dimming.
the pitch drop is added in hertz rather than in octaves, so its effect is largest at low tunings.
